sentences.text: COMMON ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of the petitions under Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the petitioners State and original complainant have prayed to quash and set aside the order dated 14.07.2021 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bhuj-Kachchh in Criminal Misc.
Application No.655 of 2021, whereby the learned Session Judge has granted anticipatory bail to the original accused.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.M.T.M.Hakim with learned advocate Mr.Rizwan Shaikh for the petitioner in Criminal Misc. Application No.632 of 2022, learned APP for the State and learned advocate Mr.Ankit Shah for original accused.

3. Learned advocate Mr.Hakim for the petitioner in Criminal Misc. Application No.632 of 2022 would submit that Shah Sanjeev and Associates, Chartered Accountants who has been hired by Khoja Shia Isna-Ishari Jamat-Kera for Forensic Accounting and Investigation Report filed entire report and based on summary of said report, FIR has been filed before the concerned Police Station involving transaction of huge amount of Wakf Board

. He would submit that learned Sessions Judge while granting anticipatory bail to the accused has not taken into consideration this report produced at Annexure E (page no.99) as well as FIR accompanied by said report whereby it is alleged that huge financial irregularity of Rs.8 Crores has been made which pertains to Wakf.
He would submit that learned Sessions Judge without considering gravity of offence and other material on record, on untenable grounds granted anticipatory bail to the accused.
Therefore, it is submitted that petition deserves consideration.
It is also submitted that in all three antecedent are registered against the accused which is not considered by the learned Sessions Judge while granting anticipatory bail the accused.
3.1 Upon above submission, learned advocate Mr.Hakim submitted to allow the petition.

4. Joining submission of learned advocate Mr.Hakim, learned APP for the State who is also seeking cancellation of bail has taken this Court through the contention raised by the learned PP before the learned Trial Court and submitted that before the learned Trial Court various transactions have been displayed but learned Sessions Judge while granting anticipatory bail to the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21918/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined accused did not consider this aspect and dealt with this issue on the reasoning that these are financial irregularities and therefore, order is cryptic and non-reasoned.
Thus, it is submitted that impugned order is required to be quashed and set aside.

5. Opposing cancellation of bail applications, learned advocate Mr.Shah for the accused took this Court through page no.61 (page no.26 of internal bail order) to submit that learned Trial Court has recorded two aspects, at first point of time summary report was filed for identical offence against accused but anyhow later on, FIR is registered.
Secondly, entire dispute pertains to documentary evidence and they are lying with Investigating Officer.

Not only that parties have chequered history inter-se fighting with each other in seizing of Wakf and it is part of long lasting dispute between the parties and therefore, learned Trial Court who has granted anticipatory bail on 14.07.2021 to the accused should not be disturbed.
It is submitted that no case is made out where it can be said that the accused have misused their personal liberty.
Thus, it is submitted to dismiss the petitions.

6. Having heard learned advocates for the parties and perusing the papers, at the outset, it is to be noted that offence against the accused is registered with concerned Police Station is with regard to section 406 and section 420 of IPC.
Maximum punishment which can be imposed on successful conviction is upto 7 years.

In such kind of cases, whether arrest is to be made or not has been discussed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar v/s. State of Bihar [(2003 (8) SCC 273] NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21918/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined and specific guidelines are issued.

So ordinarily, in case of offence under section 406 and section 420 of IPC, arrest is not to be made unless specific grounds are canvassed before the learned Trial Court that further investigation of the case can be made only if accused are in custody.
7. At this juncture, I am refer reasoning and finding given by the learned Trial Court while enlarging accused on bail.

Internal Translated version of internal page no.26 of the impugned order reads as under :-
"Thus, after reading all the documentary evidences and police papers produced in this matter and along with the same, if the statement of Ankit Choksi, Chartered Accountant recorded before the Ahmedabad Police and the report of Sanjiv Shah,
Chartered Accountant Forensic Accounting and Investigation are read, the allegation made against the present applicants/ accused persons prima facie appear to be merely of irregularities.

Further, as stated by the complainant, the present applicants/ accused persons have committed fraud and embezzlement in the accounts, therefore, instead of the police custody, the investigation of this fact can also be carried out using the records of the Trust and Jamat.
At present, the applicants/ accused persons does not appear to be the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21918/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined Trustees or the Administrators of the Trust.
In such circumstances, there is no possibility that they may temper with the accounts books or the financial record.
Thus, there is a dispute between both the parties regarding the accounts.
This dispute was also heard in the Waqf Board and all the Muslim Organizations are governed by the Waqf Board.

Thus,
considering the provision of the Waqf Act; provision of Section 438 of the Criminal Procedure Code; the allegations made against the applicants/ accused persons; the penal provisions of the Sections 406, 420, 114 of the I.P.C. and considering the Judgements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arneshkumar and Siddaram Mahtre,
offense regarding financial accounts has been registered against the applicants/
accused persons and as the same rely on the documentary evidence, prima facie it does not appear that, police custody is required for the interrogation of the applicants / accused persons in regard with the said offence.
The present applicants / accused persons are giving assurance of their co-operation whenever they are summoned by the police for the investigation.

Therefore, in such circumstances, as the applicants /
accused persons are permanently residing at the address mentioned in the application and as they are giving assurance of abiding by all such conditions that may be imposed by the Hon'ble Court, the case of the applicants / accused persons appears to be fit for release on bail.

In such circumstances, as this court deem fit to release the applicants/ accused persons on bail by using discretionary powers, below order is passed granting the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21918/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined said bail application subject to the conditions."
8.
Learned Sessions Judge has noted that there is allegation of huge financial irregularities.
Allegation of forgery or siphoning of amount is to be decided after trial between the parties.

sentences.text: Proceedings are going on.
Evidence are in documentary format and lying with the Wakf Board and police.
These reasons have weighed learned Sessions Judge to grant anticipatory bail to the accused.
According to this Court, no error has been crept in the impugned order.
Denying bail at the first instance is another thing and cancellation of bail already granted is altogether different.

Person seeking cancellation of bail has to establish before this Court that order of learned Trial Court is perverse and against settled principle of law or irrelevant or extraneous consideration or there are supervising circumstances or breach of condition.
The Court cannot mechanically cancel bail as issue involves personal liberty of person.

9. In the case of Bhagirathsinh Jadeja v/s. State Of Gujarat [1984 (1) SCC 284], the Hon'ble Apex Court in para 6 has held as under :-
"6.

entities.text: Bhagirathsinh Jadeja v/s. State Of Gujarat [1984 (1) SCC 284]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In our opinion, the learned Judge appears to have misdirected himself while examining the question of directing cancellation of bail by interfering with a discretionary order made by the learned Sessions Judge.

One could have appreciated the anxiety of the learned Judge of the High Court that in the circumstances found by him that the victim attacked was a social and political NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/21918/2021 ORDER DATED: 16/02/2024 undefined worker and therefore the accused should not be granted bail but we fail to appreciate how that circumstance should be considered so overriding as to permit interference with a discretionary order of the learned Sessions Judge granting bail.
The High Court completely overlooked the fact that it was not for it to decide whether the bail should be granted but the application before it was for cancellation of the bail.
Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order seeking cancellation of the bail.

And the trend today is towards granting bail because it is now well-settled by a catena of decisions of this Court that the power to grant bail is not to be exercised as if the punishment before trial is being imposed.

The only material considerations in such a situation are whether the accused would be readily available for his trial and whether he is likely to abuse the discretion granted in his favour by tampering with evidence.
The order made by the High Court is conspicuous by its silence on these two relevant considerations.

It is for these reasons that we consider in the interest of justice a compelling necessity to interfere with the order made by the High Court."
10.
Resultantly, present petitions fails and stands dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
